children: The valuation premium of the U.S.'s tech
giants has nearly vanished as massive capital expenditures and rising borrowing costs drag their price-to-earnings ratios down to the broader market average, according to Goldman Sachs Research.
A combination of a higher cost of capital and increased capital intensity is actively suppressing the future cash flow values of dominant tech hyperscalers
, Goldman wrote in a note published Thursday.
This financial pressure has triggered a significant valuation de-rating among the market's heaviest hitters, as the 12-month forward P/E multiple for the top five largest stocks in the S&P 500
has declined markedly from its recent peaks.

After trading at a massive premium over the past several years, the valuations of these mega-cap firms are now converging closely with the average forward P/E of the other 495 stocks in the index, suggesting that current large-cap valuations are far less demanding than the market historically perceives.

title: Valuation gap closes on Wall Street's heaviest hitters - Goldman
